3.
ORAL COMMUNICATIONS AND MEETING ATTENDANCE REPORTS FROM THE CITY COUNCIL
The City Council may discuss and act upon items described under Council Comments; however, items which are not will be limited to Council reports, announcements, or requests for clarification, or factual information, or to placement of matters on the agenda for a future meeting.
4.
ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
Persons wishing to speak on Consent Agenda items or subjects other than those scheduled are requested to do so at this time. When addressing the Council, please come to the podium and give your name and address for the record. In order to conduct a timely meeting, a 5 minute time limit per person has been established. Amendments to Government Code Section 54954.2 prohibit the Council from taking action or engaging in discussion on a specific item unless it appears on a posted agenda.
5.
CONSENT AGENDA
All items under the Consent Agenda are considered by the Council to be routine and will be enacted by one motion in the form listed below. MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE LOMITA CITY COUNCIL
  June 4, 2012

1. OPENING CEREMONIES

  a. Call Meeting to Order

A regular meeting of the Lomita City Council was called to order at 7 p.m. on Monday,
June 4, 2012, in the Council Chambers, Lomita City Hall, 24300 Narbonne Avenue.

  b. Flag Salute

Mayor Gazeley led the salute to the flag.

  c. Invocation

Councilmember Sanchez gave the invocation.

  d. Roll Call

Those responding to roll call by Assistant City Clerk Shumway were
COUNCILMEMBERS: Estrada, Sanchez, Savidan, Traina, and Mayor Gazeley. Also
present were Interim City Manager Sugano, Public Works Director Damasse, City
Attorney Hogin, and Assistant City Clerk Shumway.

2. PRESENTATIONS

Mayor Gazeley and Councilmembers presented a Certificate of Recognition to Michael
Graf for receiving the Outstanding Older American Award.

Mayor Gazeley and Members of the City Council, with the aid of Public Safety and
Traffic Commissioner Jankowski, presented Certificates of Recognition to the winners
and sponsors of the poster and slogan contest associated with the "Follow Me, I am
Gang and Drug Free" walk.

3. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS AND MEETING ATTENDANCE REPORTS FROM THE CITY
  COUNCIL

Mayor Gazeley introduced new City Manager Michael Rock. Mr. Rock stated that it was
a pleasure to be here and that he was looking forward to working for the City of Lomita.

Mayor Gazeley requested a future agenda item for the creation of a Council ad hoc
committee to review the Cypress reservoir issues. Councilmember Sanchez seconded
the motion, which carried unanimously.

  June 4, 2012 Council Minutes  Page 1 of 4
 Councilmember Traina requested a future agenda item for discussion of reservoir
issues with Water Works, the City’s current water operations contractor relative to the
Cypress Water Production Facility. Councilmember Sanchez and Savidan agreed that it
would be a beneficial topic for future discussion. Mayor Gazeley agreed.

Councilmember Traina stated that this was his second request to staff regarding the
inconsistencies he identified between the City’s letters mailed to Lomita residents that
indicated 100% of well water was distributed during the 2010 reservoir trial period, while
daily production of water pumped in 2010 was twice less than the required 132 million of
gallons of water. According to Councilmember Traina, the discrepancy suggests that
water blending had already occurred and he asked staff to respond. Interim City
Manager Gary Sugano stated that staff will provide that information.

Councilmember Traina inquired as to who authorized the content of the letter mailed to
Lomita residents in response to Mr. Albert’s letter to residents, and what were the
mailing costs of the letter. Councilmember Traina further added that the information in
the City's letter was not a true representation of the issues. Interim City Manager
Sugano responded that it was staff’s decision to reply to Mr. Albert’s letter, and was part
of the public outreach process authorized earlier by the Council.

Councilmember Traina expressed his displeasure with the double standard that Council
demonstrated during the City Council meeting on May 21, 2012, by engaging in
dialogue with the Water Replenishment District Director, but not allowing Council any
dialogue with members of the public. City Attorney Hogin explained that in accordance
with the Brown Act, the intent of oral communications on the agenda is to allow
members of the public to bring forward issues that are not agendized. City Attorney
Hogin further stated that the City Council cannot engage in discussion or take action on
non-agendized items; however, Council is allowed to ask questions for purposes of
clarification or to refer the matter back to staff.

Councilmember Traina expressed his discontent that consultants were paid $10,000 to
conduct the community outreach meeting regarding the water rate increase, which he
thought could have been done by staff, and in turn save money for the City. Interim City
Manager Sugano responded that the consultants' fees of $10,000 covered the entire
public outreach program, not just the meeting itself.

Lastly, Councilmember Traina thanked Mr. Albert for all the hard work he put into
researching the reservoir issues.

Mayor Gazeley invited Councilmembers and staff to attend an upcoming meeting on
earthquake preparedness so as to learn how to minimize impacts in case of an
earthquake.

4. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

Fred Adjarian, Golden State Water Company District Manager, introduced himself as the
new District Manager for Golden State, and added that he is looking forward to working

  June 4, 2012 Council Minutes  Page 2 of 4
 with staff on the ground water lease.

Martin Spain, Lomita resident, was appalled with the personnel costs of the Public
Works Department and urged City Council to contract out City of Lomita water services.

Joe McGrath, Lomita resident, was concerned with salary allocations to the Water
Enterprise Fund, and pointed out that revenues collected should only support
operations and expenses associated with the fund, and exclude General Fund
expenditures such as police, fire, etc. Mr. McGrath requested a review of Enterprise
Fund allocations. Mr. McGrath also asked City Council to hire a neutral third party to
investigate allegations brought up by some City employees that were published in The
Daily Breeze on June 2, 2012.

Ben Porter, Lomita resident, asked City Council to consider allowing residents to vote on
the water rate increase, and to allow for more public participation in the decision
regarding water rate increases and reservoir issues.

Lawson Pedigo, Lomita resident, agreed with Mr. Ben Porter and asked City Council to
have residents vote on water rate increases before the increases take place.

George Kivett, Lomita resident, talked about the importance of freedom of speech and
allowing speakers to express their opinions during the oral communications section on
the agenda. According to Mr. Kivett, the US Chamber, Cal Chamber, and the Lomita
Chamber of Commerce received an anonymous letter concerning oppression of public
speech at City Council meetings. Mr. Kivett further added that City staff should not
discourage people from speaking up on any issues.

Cindy Segawa, Lomita resident, asked City Council to consider including President
Avenue Elementary School, located in Harbor City, into the “Follow Me, I’m Gang and
Drug Free” walk, since one third of Lomita kids attend that school.

Dave Albert, Lomita resident, alleged that there was illegal activity going on at the
reservoir, and that water blending had already occurred in 2010. Mr. Albert added that
according to his conversations with staff, water blending did not work after staff tried
everything they could.

Mr. Albert distributed a copy of an invoice from Water Works that indicated chemicals
were purchased in February 2012, before the City Council meeting on March 5, 2012,
where the City Council made a decision to authorize water blending. Mr. Albert stated
that this could be in violation of the Brown Act due to the fact that staff could not
proceed with water blending until it was authorized by City Council.

Sharon Houston, Lomita resident, asked staff to put an exact date, month, and year on
any letters sent out by the City. Ms. Houston also stated that there is a deficit of
$275,000 in the budget, which is due to the City’s bond obligations, and she asked City
staff to actively pursue grant opportunities to reduce the deficit and increase revenues,

  June 4, 2012 Council Minutes  Page 3 of 4
 including applying for water conservation grants through the West Basin Municipal
District.

5. CONSENT AGENDA

  a. Motion to Waive Further Reading.

  b. Recommendation to approve the minutes for the City Council Meeting and the
  Adjourned City Council Meeting held on May 21, 2012.

  c. Approval of Demands - Resolution 2012-24.

  d. Report dealing with economic development activities.

  e. Report dealing with activities of the Parks Department.

  f. Report dealing with activities of the Public Works Department.

  g. Report presenting the Treasurer’s Report.

  h. Report granting the lease of 450 acre feet of the City’s water pumping rights to
  Golden State Water Company, and authorize the Interim City Manager to sign a
  lease agreement with Golden State Water Company.

  i. Report recommending approval of the assessment for the annual maintenance,
  operation, and servicing of the parkway landscaping along the north side of Palos
  Verdes Drive North (Landscape Maintenance District No.1), and the resolution
  approving the engineer’s report and confirming the assessment for 2012/13. –
  Resolution 2012-23

Interim City Manager Sugano stated that staff provided City Council with revised
minutes, in which the changes were highlighted. Councilmember Estrada moved to
approve the consent agenda and minutes with corrections. Councilmember Sanchez
seconded the motion. Councilmember Traina pointed out some additional corrections to
the minutes. The motion carried unanimously.

ADJOURNMENT

Meeting adjourned at 8:09 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,

_________________________
Lena Shumway, CMC
Assistant City Clerk

  June 4, 2012 Council Minutes  Page 4 of 4
